# Blueprint

> Get repetitive work done by robots. A site films one job that repeats, once, or starts with a description. Blueprint sends the job, as a job packet (what the job is, a first look at which robots could fit, and the simulation of the site once it is built), to the robot deployment companies it approves, so they can tell the site if they can do it. A site's name, address and contact details go to a company only when the site asks for an introduction. Free for sites.

The job packet holds the site's own sentence for the job and a first look on paper (the robot most likely to fit, from published specifications and where it has been used). Blueprint uses video to build a simulation of the site when it can. When Blueprint can't build a simulation for a kind of job yet, the job still goes to companies; its simulation waits until Blueprint can build one, and the first look stays on the job page.

Blueprint sends each job automatically to the deployment companies it has approved. The job packet gives the site's description, a first look at which robots could fit, and what counts as done when known. When the site sends video, the packet includes it without sound and adds the simulation when it is ready. A company answers "Interested", "Not a fit" or "Would need something"; once the job's simulation can be downloaded, it can also answer "Tested it: can do" or "Tested it: cannot yet". Blueprint can't promise any will say yes. After a company answers "Interested" or "Tested it: can do", the site can ask for an introduction to each company it wants to meet. After an introduction the company gets the site's name, address and contact details, and the site gets the company's name and contact details. Any work is agreed between the site and the company. Nothing is charged today. A simulation is a bounded estimate and never certifies physical performance or safety.

Deployment companies apply on the page for deployment companies. Applications stay pending until Blueprint approves the company by hand; applying does not grant access or promise a job. Contact: hello@tryblueprint.io.

## Evidence boundary

Customer wording uses “job” for the work a site wants automated and “task” for the specific robot action and its technical conditions. API fields and identifiers retain their existing names.

A Task Evaluation Run returns a decision or abstention. Pipeline owns method qualification and routing; physical outcomes remain distinct from simulation and generated evidence.
